key_insight: HARMONI combines multimodal perception, long-term user memory, and LLM-based reasoning to enable socially assistive robots to personalize and adapt interactions across multiple users over time.
problem_solved: Existing HRI systems struggle to sustain personalized behavior and dynamically adapt in multi-user, real-world settings; HARMONI addresses persistent user modeling and context-aware social adaptation for long-term multi-user interactions.
method: Multimodal perception: identifies active speaker(s) and extracts audio, visual, and behavioral cues for contextual understanding.
Long-term personalized memory: maintains and updates multi-user profiles and interaction history to inform future behavior.
LLM-driven reasoning & policy: uses large language models to fuse context and user profiles into socially appropriate dialogue plans and action policies for the robot.
impact: Provides a practical blueprint for integrating LLMs into robotic agents that require sustained personalization and social adaptability, improving long-term engagement and real-world deployment potential for ML-driven HRI.
visual_elements: End-to-end system diagram showing Perception → Memory → LLM Reasoning → Policy/Execution loop
Interaction timeline illustrating accumulation of user preferences and personalization across repeated sessions
Before/after comparison chart (engagement, satisfaction, or task success) showing benefits of personalization
Annotated example multimodal turn (audio + gaze + gesture) mapped to model input and resulting robot response
paper_title: HARMONI: Multimodal Personalization of Multi-User Human-Robot Interactions with LLMs
paper_authors: Jeanne Malécot, Hamed Rahimi, Jeanne Cattoni, Marie Samson, Mouad Abrini
